traits.height_max_m.note: Jepson (1925), as P. rivularis: grows 3.05 m to 9.14 m tall (converted from feet).

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Malus fusca (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.68 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.69, branches 0.64. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.path_half.note: A choice of the model's (crown form step B, broadleaf revision 11): the wood from the base at which a shoot's nodes are half as long, fitted so the plant grows to the height of its oldest reference size, with the crown's width left to grow inside the loose region.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a small, thicket-forming tree with crooked branches, alternate toothed leaves and clusters of white to pink flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 8 m tall at 30 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: green leaves; white flowers flushed pink; grey-brown, scaly bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: clusters of little apples 1 to 1.5 cm long on long stalks, green turning yellow and red. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) is authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: pinkish-white flowers in April and May; little apples green in summer, yellow to red in August and September, hanging into November. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): grey to reddish-brown bark, smooth, then scaly and fissured; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): sun leaves a little smaller and narrower than shade leaves; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): white or blush flowers 15 to 20 mm across with about 20 stamens, in clusters of 6 to 12 drawn opening together (in apples the central flower opens a few days before the rest). From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on the inferior ovary, twenty stamens and a pistil of three carpels, from the characters of its own, Rosaceae's and Malus's by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Pyrus rivularis: carpels commonly 3. The Burke Herbarium (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): usually 3 styles (or 4), joined in the lower third.
